cards.text: The LORD is speaking through His prophet Isaiah, and He's calling the islands and the peoples into court. Let them come forward and testify, He says, and let us draw near together for judgment. Friend, the islands just got a summons, and I bet nobody wants to take the stand first.

cards.question: Court is called. Before the islands say a word, the LORD tells them to be ___ before Him.

cards.text: Then the LORD puts a question to the court. Who has stirred up someone from the east and called him to his feet in righteousness?

cards.question: The one from the east is on the move. The kings in his way are subdued before him.

cards.text: Nations are turned to dust by his sword and to windblown chaff by his bow. Friend, I spent YEARS under the dust in a junk drawer, so trust me, I know dust, and that sword is MAKING it.

cards.question: As he chases the nations, the one from the east drags along and struggles to keep up.

cards.text: He goes on safely, hardly touching the path with his feet, like me when the oven timer goes off and my gold base is barely TOUCHING the floor. Then the LORD asks: who has performed this and carried it out, calling forth the generations from the beginning?

cards.question: Someone is behind all of this, calling forth the generations from the beginning. Who is it?

cards.text: The LORD asks the question and answers it Himself: He is the first and the last. Friend, that's not a question, that's a MIC DROP, and the islands are watching the whole thing.

cards.question: The islands see what the LORD has done, and they ___.
The ends of the earth tremble, and they come forward. As they do, what does each one say to his brother?

cards.text: The craftsman encourages the goldsmith, and the one with the hammer cheers the one who strikes the anvil, saying of the welding, "It is good." Friend, I have NEVER had a coworker hype my work like that.

cards.question: The crew wants the thing they've made to stand firm. What do they do to it?

cards.text: Now the LORD turns from the islands to His own people. He calls Israel His servant, Jacob, the one He has chosen, descendant of Abraham.

cards.question: When the LORD mentions Abraham, Israel's ancestor, what does He call him?

cards.text: He brought Israel from the ends of the earth and called them from its farthest corners. Friend, the ends of the earth were TREMBLING a minute ago, and that's exactly where the LORD went to get His people.

cards.question: The LORD tells Israel He chose them, but then He rejected them.

cards.text: Now comes the line people write on sticky notes and slap on the bathroom mirror. Twice in one verse, the LORD tells Israel not to be afraid.

cards.question: The LORD tells Israel not to fear. What reason does He give them?
Besides being with them, the LORD says He will ___ Israel and surely help them.

cards.text: And He will uphold Israel with His righteous right hand. Friend, I spent years propped up by a stack of old takeout menus, so believe me, that is a WHOLE different level of support.

cards.question: Next the LORD speaks about all who rage against Israel. What will happen to them?

answers.text: They will be ashamed and disgraced

cards.question: Israel will go looking for their enemies and will not find them.

cards.text: Those who wage war against Israel will come to nothing. It's like looking for the car that cut you off, right there at the next red light, and it's just GONE.
Because He is the LORD their God, the One who takes hold of their right hand. And He tells them again not to fear, because He will help them.
Then the LORD calls out, "Do not fear, O Jacob, you worm, O few men of Israel." Friend, I lived in the back of a junk drawer for years, so the worm? I GET the worm.

cards.question: The LORD promises to help the few men of Israel. Who does He say is their Redeemer?

cards.text: Then the worm gets a promotion: the LORD will make Israel into a threshing sledge. Worm to heavy farm equipment in the very NEXT verse, friend, and it took me YEARS just to get out of a drawer.

cards.question: The threshing sledge the LORD makes out of Israel is old and dull.

cards.text: New and sharp, with many teeth, and it threshes the mountains and turns the hills to chaff. Going from worn down to new and sharp? Friend, that's my WHOLE story.

cards.question: A wind carries the chaff away and a gale scatters it. What does Israel do then?

cards.text: Then the picture changes. The poor and needy look for water, but there is none, and their tongues are parched with thirst.

cards.question: The LORD will leave the thirsty poor and needy to find water on their own.

cards.text: They're looking for water, and the LORD's answer is RIVERS on the barren heights and fountains in the middle of the valleys. That's like looking for one napkin and getting handed the whole warehouse.

cards.question: The LORD will also turn the ___ into a pool of water.

cards.text: Then the LORD plants cedars, acacias, myrtles and olive trees in the wilderness, and sets cypresses, elms and boxwood together in the desert. Friend, I can't keep ONE little plant alive on my bakery windowsill.

cards.question: Rivers in the desert and trees in the wilderness. Why does the LORD do all of this?

answers.text: So all will know the LORD did it
So Israel can build new cities
So the nations will fear Israel

findings.problem: The joke compares nations being turned to dust by a sword with Papa Dorin lying under dust in the drawer. Being covered in dust is not the same action as being made into dust, so the comparison doesn't click. It also makes a punchline out of nations being destroyed.

rule.text: 2. The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The question gives only that the ends of the earth tremble and come forward. It leaves out the detail from verse 6 that each one helps the other. With fear as the only context, 'Flee for your life' or 'We are finished' is as reasonable as 'Be strong', so the baker can only get it right by luck.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: Verse 7 shows the frightened nations' craftsmen welding a made object and nailing it down so it will not topple. The previous passage (Isaiah 40:19-20) shows this object is an idol, and the passage contrasts it with the LORD. The walkthrough never says what is being built, and the joke ('I have NEVER had a coworker hype my work like that') presents the work as admirable. The baker can miss the point of verses 5-7.
findings.question: In Isaiah 41:7, should Papa Dorin say the craftsmen are making an idol, citing Isaiah 40:19-20? The docs allow filling in what the text clearly implies and using outside facts with their reference. They also say to leave open what the text leaves open, and verse 7 never says 'idol'.

findings.problem: The car comparison is muddled. 'Looking for the car that cut you off, right there at the next red light, and it's just GONE' first says the car is right there and then says it's gone. A stranger would have to reread it to see the joke.

rule.text: 4. It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: 'Then the LORD plants cedars... and sets cypresses...' tells the planting as something happening now. Verse 19 is a promise ('I will plant', 'I will set'). Every other card in this stop keeps the future 'will'.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Most of the jokes are the same kind: a junk-drawer or renewal callback about Papa Dorin himself (stop 1 card 5, stop 2 card 8, stop 3 cards 1, 3 and 5). Three of these come in a row in stop 3. The repetition reads like a formula, not like jokes that fit each moment.

rule.text: No formula. His personality fits whatever moment he's in, whether it's a tense moment in a story, a hard teaching or a quick question. There are no joke quotas and no required kinds of jokes.
